title: Residue differential coordinates preserve independent cotangent classes
statement: Write R=k[y_1,...,y_m], p=φ^{-1}(m_A), and A_0=R_p. Let ψ:A_0→A be any local ring homomorphism whose restriction to R is φ. For any subset s of m_0=maximalIdeal(A_0), if the classes of its elements in m_0/m_0² are linearly independent over K_0=κ(A_0), then the classes of their ψ-images in m_A/m_A² are linearly independent over K=κ(A). The hypotheses are: k has characteristic pchar>0; A is a Noetherian local k-algebra geometrically regular over k [def-weil-pbc-g-ring]; F is a finitely generated intermediate field k⊆F⊆κ(A) [def-pc-field-extension]; φ:R→A is a k-algebra map [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]; its residue images a_i lie in F and the differentials da_i form an F-basis of Ω[F/k] [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]. Cotangent classes mean z modulo the square of the maximal ideal, and linear independence means every finite relation with residue-field coefficients is trivial. The image of z∈m_0 lies in m_A because ψ is local [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], so the comparison is well-defined [def-weil-regular-scheme].

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07E6, proof (lines 8866-8894), from the construction of A_0 to injectivity of the right vertical cotangent comparison; https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/07E6

proof.text: *Setup.* Put $R=k[y_1,\dots,y_m]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] and $\mathfrak p=\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak m)$, a prime ideal of $R$. Every $s\in R\setminus\mathfrak p$ has $\varphi(s)\notin\mathfrak m$, a unit of the local ring $A$, so $\varphi$ extends uniquely to $\varphi_0:A_0:=R_{\mathfrak p}\to A$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], a local homomorphism ($\varphi_0^{-1}(\mathfrak m)=\mathfrak pR_{\mathfrak p}=:\mathfrak m_0$). $R$ is Noetherian (finite type over the field $k$, which is Noetherian) [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian], [lem-weil-pbc-field-regular-ring], hence so is $A_0$ [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian]; $A_0$ is a Noetherian local ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Its residue field $K_0=A_0/\mathfrak m_0=\operatorname{Frac}(R/\mathfrak p)$ embeds into $K$ via $\varphi_0$; it is generated as a field over $k$ by the classes $\bar y_i$, which lie in $F$ by hypothesis, so $k\subseteq K_0\subseteq F\subseteq K$. Finally $\mathfrak pA=\mathfrak m_0A$ (the ideal generated by $\varphi_0(\mathfrak m_0)$), so $A/\mathfrak pA=A/\mathfrak m_0A$.

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 07E6 (lemma-geometrically-regular-over-field, lines 8866-8894): 'Set A_0 = k[y_1,...,y_m]_p with maximal ideal m_0 and residue field K_0'

proof.text: *Differentials of $A_0$.* $\Omega_{R/k}$ is free with basis $\mathrm dy_1,\dots,\mathrm dy_m$ [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-kahler-basis] and $\Omega_{A_0/k}\cong(\Omega_{R/k})_{\mathfrak p}$ [lem-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials-localization], so $\Omega_{A_0/k}$ is free of rank $m$ with basis $\mathrm dy_i$ [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]. The map $w_0:\Omega_{A_0/k}\otimes_{A_0}K_0\to\Omega_{K_0/k}$, $\mathrm dy_i\otimes1\mapsto\mathrm d\bar y_i$, is surjective since $A_0\to K_0$ is surjective [lem-weil-pbc-jacobi-zariski-differential-maps]. It is injective: if $\sum c_i\,\mathrm d\bar y_i=0$ in $\Omega_{K_0/k}$ with $c_i\in K_0$, apply the $K_0$-linear map $\Omega_{K_0/k}\to\Omega_{F/k}$ induced by $K_0\subseteq F$ (functoriality of $\Omega$); it gives $\sum c_i\,\mathrm d\bar y_i=0$ in $\Omega_{F/k}$, where the $\mathrm d\bar y_i$ form an $F$-basis by hypothesis, so all $c_i=0$. Hence $w_0$ is an isomorphism (both sides of dimension $m$).

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 07E6 (lemma-geometrically-regular-over-field, lines 8866-8894): 'Note that Omega_{A_0/k} is free of rank m and Omega_{A_0/k} (x) K_0 -> Omega_{K_0/k} is an isomorphism' (the source gives no argument; written out here)

proof.text: For every finite purely inseparable k'/k, k'⊗_k R is the polynomial ring over k' by [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-scalar-extension]. It is regular directly by Mathlib MvPolynomial.isRegularRing_of_isRegularRing, the existing leaf [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-field-regular-ring]. Localization base change identifies k'⊗_k A_0 with a localization of this regular polynomial ring. The already-proved source instance IsRegularRing.localization proves regularity of that localization; no smooth-ascent lemma is used. Hence A_0 is geometrically regular [def-weil-pbc-g-ring].

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 07E6 (lemma-geometrically-regular-over-field, lines 8866-8894): 'It is clear that A_0 is geometrically regular over k' (the source gives no argument; written out here)

proof.text: *For $A_0$ the canonical map is an isomorphism.* By [lem-weil-pbc-geometrically-regular-h1-injective] (Proposition 07E5, (1)$\Rightarrow$(3)) applied to $A_0$ (step 3): $A_0$ is a regular local ring [def-weil-regular-scheme] and $c_0:H_1(L_{K_0/k})\to\mathfrak m_0/\mathfrak m_0^2$ is injective. The Jacobi-Zariski sequence of $k\to A_0\to K_0$ [lem-weil-pbc-jacobi-zariski-homology-sequence] contains the exact piece $H_1(L_{K_0/k})\xrightarrow{v}H_1(L_{K_0/A_0})\xrightarrow{\partial}\Omega_{A_0/k}\otimes_{A_0}K_0\xrightarrow{w_0}\Omega_{K_0/k}$, where $v$ is the map induced by $k[K_0]\to A_0[K_0]$, i.e. the map whose composite with $H_1(L_{K_0/A_0})\cong\mathfrak m_0/\mathfrak m_0^2$ [lem-weil-pbc-jacobi-zariski-surjection-h1] is $c_0$ (the definition in [lem-weil-pbc-geometrically-regular-h1-injective]). As $w_0$ is injective (step 2), $\partial=0$, so $v$ and hence $c_0$ is surjective. Thus $c_0$ is an isomorphism of $K_0$-vector spaces.

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 07E6 (lemma-geometrically-regular-over-field, lines 8866-8894): 'Hence H_1(L_{K_0/k}) -> m_0/m_0^2 is an isomorphism, see Proposition 07E5' (surjectivity, from the Jacobi-Zariski sequence and step 2, is left implicit in the source)

proof.text: *The square.* Consider the square of $K$-linear maps with top $c_0\otimes K:H_1(L_{K_0/k})\otimes_{K_0}K\to\mathfrak m_0/\mathfrak m_0^2\otimes_{K_0}K$, bottom $c:H_1(L_{K/k})\to\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2$ (the canonical map for $A$), left $a$ induced by $k[K_0]\to k[K]$, and right $\mu:\bar x\otimes\lambda\mapsto\lambda\overline{\varphi_0(x)}$. It commutes: both composites $H_1(L_{K_0/k})\to H_1(L_{K/A})$ are induced by morphisms of presentations $k[K_0]\to A[K]$ over the square $k\to A$, $K_0\subseteq K$ (namely $k[K_0]\to A_0[K_0]\to A[K]$ and $k[K_0]\to k[K]\to A[K]$), hence agree [lem-weil-pbc-nl-presentation-h1-functoriality] (1),(2); and the morphism $A_0[K_0]\to A[K]$ is compatible with the isomorphisms $H_1(L_{K_0/A_0})\cong\mathfrak m_0/\mathfrak m_0^2$ and $H_1(L_{K/A})\cong\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2$ of [lem-weil-pbc-jacobi-zariski-surjection-h1] (choose the section $\sigma$ for $A\to K$ extending $\varphi_0\circ\sigma_0$ on $K_0$; then $g\mapsto\sigma(g)$ is $\varphi_0$ applied to $g\mapsto\sigma_0(g)$), which turns $H_1(L_{K_0/A_0})\to H_1(L_{K/A})$ into $\mu$. The left map $a$ is injective by [lem-weil-pbc-transitivity-gamma] (Lemma 07E2, for $k\subseteq K_0\subseteq K$), and $c$ is injective by [lem-weil-pbc-geometrically-regular-h1-injective] applied to $A$, which also gives that $A$ is a regular local ring. Since $c_0\otimes K$ is an isomorphism (step 4) and $c\circ a=\mu\circ(c_0\otimes K)$ is injective, $\mu$ is injective.

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 07E6 (lemma-geometrically-regular-over-field, lines 8866-8894): 'Now consider [the square] ... Since the left vertical arrow is injective by Lemma 07E2 and the lower horizontal by Proposition 07E5 we conclude that the right vertical one is too' (commutativity of the square is left implicit in the source)

proof.text: An independent family in m_0/m_0² remains independent after scalar extension K_0→K (a field extension is flat, or tensor the family's free-module injection). Apply the injective cotangent comparison from step 5. It sends 1⊗[z] to [ψ(z)], so these classes are independent over K. For an arbitrary independent set, this says every finite relation is trivial, proving the stated LinearIndepOn assertion, including the empty set.

theorem linearIndepOn_of_residue_differential_basis
    (k : Type u) (A : Type v) [Field k] [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
    [IsLocalRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] (pchar : ℕ) [Fact pchar.Prime] [CharP k pchar]
    (hreg : IsGeometricallyRegular k A)
    (F : IntermediateField k (IsLocalRing.ResidueField A)) (hF : F.FG)
    (m : ℕ) (φ : MvPolynomial (Fin m) k →ₐ[k] A)
    (a : Fin m → F)
    (ha : ∀ i : Fin m, (a i : IsLocalRing.ResidueField A) =
      IsLocalRing.residue A (φ (MvPolynomial.X i)))
    (b : Module.Basis (Fin m) F (KaehlerDifferential k F))
    (hb : ∀ i : Fin m, b i = KaehlerDifferential.D k F (a i)) :
    let p := (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A).comap φ.toRingHom
    ∀ (ψ : Localization.AtPrime p →+* A) [IsLocalHom ψ],
      ψ.comp (algebraMap (MvPolynomial (Fin m) k) (Localization.AtPrime p)) =
        φ.toRingHom →
      ∀ s : Set (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (Localization.AtPrime p)),
        LinearIndepOn (IsLocalRing.ResidueField (Localization.AtPrime p))
          (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (Localization.AtPrime p)).toCotangent s →
        LinearIndepOn (IsLocalRing.ResidueField A)
          (fun x : IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (Localization.AtPrime p) ↦
            (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A).toCotangent
            ⟨ψ x, map_nonunit ψ x x.2⟩) s
